clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work, then separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. Your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979, where things settled.

clusters.name: Odette's bedrest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bedrest in the spring of 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with her over how she kept it; and your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. Your sister Ines was born in September, and by then the household had settled into a new balance.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the next decade: your grandfather Ambrose overfunctioned, taking over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her; he and your uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather developed chest pains; your grandmother fell and needed a frame; your mother overfunctioned, taking her to the clinic twice a week; your aunt Mavis came to nurse her; your father drank most evenings; and he and your mother fought over his evenings at his parents' house. Your grandmother moved to the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997, where the period settled.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for work up north in May 1999: your father argued with him over his plans and then missed days at work, sitting up late in the garage; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away and took your sister Ines with her everywhere; Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother pulled toward Ines. By August 2000, Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams, and the household had settled.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; your anxiety rose and your functioning fell. By November you took a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again, where things settled.
